allObjections.title: Axis overlap creates double-counting
allObjections.detail: CA-15-A defines a UI/UX axis in the 7-axis rubric that is 'distinct from §10.1 UI/UX' but both feed into §7.6 scoring with equal weight. This creates a double-counting problem where UI/UX issues get scored twice under different rubrics, artificially inflating their impact on the final score.

allObjections.title: Purpose capture timing creates race condition
allObjections.detail: CA-15-B requires purpose capture 'before any optimization cycle runs' but §7.5 ProductSSOT updates are atomic with output per §7. This creates a race where the first run must both capture purpose AND produce output atomically, but purpose capture requires crawling/inference that may fail, blocking all output.

allObjections.title: Conformance gate invalidation too aggressive
allObjections.detail: CA-15-D invalidates CEO sign-off on EVERY CA promotion, not just CAs that affect conformance testing. This means unrelated amendments (e.g., fixing a typo in §28) force re-validation of all products, creating unnecessary operational burden and potential service disruption.

allObjections.title: Legal/privacy axes lack jurisdictional clarity
allObjections.detail: CA-15-A axes 5-6 detect 'legal exposure' and 'privacy gaps' but the conformance criteria only mention 'jurisdictional inference per §1.1'. The §1.1 market definitions don't provide sufficient granularity for legal compliance detection across 190+ jurisdictions with conflicting requirements.

allObjections.title: Complexity of Multi-Dimensional Audit
allObjections.detail: The introduction of a 7-axis canonical rubric in §10.1.1 adds significant complexity to the audit process. Each axis requires precise conformance-test acceptance criteria, which may lead to increased false positives or negatives, especially in subjective areas like UI/UX and 'Other'.

allObjections.title: Purpose Capture Ambiguity
allObjections.detail: The proposal in CA-15-B for capturing purpose into ProductSSOT lacks clarity on how 'inferred' and 'synthesized' modes will accurately reflect the operator's intent. This could lead to misalignment between the product's actual purpose and its recorded purpose, especially if LLM inference is inaccurate.

allObjections.title: SSOT-Conformance Gate Rigidity
allObjections.detail: The end-stage SSOT-conformance gate in CA-15-D may introduce rigidity by blocking product deployment until conformance is achieved. This could delay time-sensitive releases and does not account for scenarios where full conformance is impractical or unnecessary.

allObjections.title: Lack of Rollback
allObjections.detail: The proposal does not provide a clear rollback strategy in case the 7-axis Multi-Dimensional Quality Audit causes unintended consequences, such as false positives or negatives, which could lead to incorrect optimization decisions. This is particularly concerning in §10.1.1 where the audit findings are folded into the §7.6 GTM Readiness scoring formula.

allObjections.title: Insufficient Testing
allObjections.detail: The proposal does not specify how the 7-axis Multi-Dimensional Quality Audit will be tested for accuracy and reliability, particularly for the 'other' axis which is extensible and may introduce variability in findings. This lack of testing could lead to inconsistent results and undermine the effectiveness of the audit.

allObjections.title: Operator Overload
allObjections.detail: The introduction of the purpose_record block in ProductSSOT and the requirement for operators to capture purpose statements may lead to operator overload, particularly if the purpose statements are complex or require significant time and effort to craft. This could lead to decreased productivity and increased errors.

allObjections.title: Complexity of Multi-Dimensional Quality Audit
allObjections.detail: The 7-axis canonical Quality Audit rubric introduces significant complexity. The mechanism for folding these findings into §7.6 GTM Readiness scoring may lead to confusion and potential misinterpretation of results. The conformance-test acceptance criterion for the 7-axis audit is too stringent and may not be achievable in practical scenarios.

allObjections.title: Ambiguity in Purpose Capture Modes
allObjections.detail: The three canonical purpose capture modes (described, inferred, synthesized) are not clearly defined. The inferred mode, which relies on LLM inference from page content, may introduce inaccuracies and biases. The synthesized mode, which combines multiple inputs, may lead to conflicting or unclear purpose statements.

allObjections.title: SSOT-Conformance Gate Overhead
allObjections.detail: The SSOT-Conformance Gate as an end-stage hard gate may introduce significant overhead and delay in the deployment pipeline. The requirement for CEO re-sign off on every CA promotion could become a bottleneck, especially in environments with frequent updates and promotions.

allObjections.title: Complexity Overload
allObjections.detail: The addition of a 7-axis Multi-Dimensional Quality Audit (CA-15-A) significantly increases the complexity of the system, potentially leading to maintenance challenges and increased risk of errors.

allObjections.title: Purpose Capture Ambiguity
allObjections.detail: The purpose capture mechanism (CA-15-B) relies heavily on LLM inference and synthesis, which may introduce inaccuracies and misalignments with the operator's actual intent.

allObjections.title: SSOT-Conformance Gate Overhead
allObjections.detail: The end-stage SSOT-Conformance Gate (CA-15-D) adds an additional layer of testing, which may introduce delays and increase the operational burden on the system.

allObjections.title: Overly complex quality audit
allObjections.detail: The 7-axis Multi-Dimensional Quality Audit in CA-15-A seems overly complex and potentially subjective. The conformance test acceptance criteria for each axis rely on precision/recall thresholds against labeled corpora, which may be difficult to create and maintain, especially for axes like 'UI/UX' and 'Other'.

allObjections.title: Purpose capture ambiguity
allObjections.detail: The purpose capture modes in CA-15-B, particularly 'inferred' and 'synthesized', rely heavily on LLM inference, which can be unreliable and lead to inaccurate or biased purpose statements. The lack of clear guidelines for LLM synthesis could result in inconsistent and unpredictable purpose capture.

allObjections.title: SSOT-conformance gate risk
allObjections.detail: The SSOT-conformance gate in CA-15-D, while intended to ensure adherence to the SSOT, could become a bottleneck in the development process. The requirement for CEO re-sign-off on every CA promotion could create delays and hinder agility, especially if the CEO is unavailable or has limited bandwidth.

allObjections.title: Extensibility axis 'Other' vague
allObjections.detail: The 'Other' axis in the Multi-Dimensional Quality Audit (CA-15-A) is a catch-all that lacks clear definition. While intended for extensibility, it could become a dumping ground for subjective or irrelevant findings, undermining the overall rigor of the audit.

allObjections.title: Purpose drift handling unclear
allObjections.detail: The handling of `PURPOSE_DRIFT` in CA-15-C is unclear. Exiting with `NO_IMPROVEMENT` and an annotation seems insufficient. A significant drift in purpose should trigger a more proactive response, such as requiring operator intervention or automatically re-running the purpose capture process.

allObjections.title: Axis set mismatches question
allObjections.detail: CA-15-A-Q1 asks to ratify a 7-axis rubric with UX, API, Data, Auth, Perf, Accessibility, Observability, but the proposal text defines axes as redundancy, grammar, syntax, UI/UX-content, legal, privacy, and other. That mismatch makes the amendment internally inconsistent with its own acceptance criterion and untestable as written.

allObjections.title: Duplicate scoring semantics
allObjections.detail: CA-15-A folds the new audit into §7.6 with the same score formula and equal footing with existing detectors, but it also says the axes are content-quality and separately says they are advisory in the legal axis. The proposal does not define how conflicts are resolved when content-quality findings, Phase A findings, and Phase B findings all overlap, so the same defect can be double-counted or suppressed depending on implementation choice.

allObjections.title: Purpose capture risks false intent
allObjections.detail: CA-15-B lets the system infer or synthesize a product's purpose from crawls or multiple sources and then stores that as canonical ProductSSOT state. That creates a high risk of ossifying a model hallucination or a marketing page's incidental text as the product's real objective, especially when the operator never supplied a precise purpose statement.

allObjections.title: Drift gate can deadlock runs
allObjections.detail: CA-15-C's PURPOSE_DRIFT semantics can exit NO_IMPROVEMENT with explicit drift annotation when the purpose changes, but it does not require a fresh operator approval path or a bounded fallback. A product whose legitimate scope changes during renewal could repeatedly fail the exit gate even after successful technical remediation, turning an optimization loop into a deadlock.

allObjections.title: CEO re-sign every CA is brittle
allObjections.detail: CA-15-D-Q2 makes CEO sign-off invalid on every CA promotion, even promotions that do not affect the specific conformance gate. This couples ordinary governance churn to a single human approver and can stall the entire pipeline over unrelated amendments, creating an availability bottleneck rather than a control mechanism.

allObjections.title: Purpose Capture Ambiguity
allObjections.detail: The three canonical purpose-capture modes (§7.5 `purpose_record`) may lead to inconsistent purpose statements. The 'inferred' mode relies on LLM inference, which may not always accurately capture the operator's intent.

allObjections.title: SSOT-Conformance Gate Timing
allObjections.detail: The §27 SSOT-Conformance Gate is placed at the end-stage, which may allow non-conformant changes to propagate through the pipeline. It should be considered to run this gate at every §11 step.

allObjections.title: §10.1.1 rubric overlaps §10.1
allObjections.detail: The 7-axis Multi-Dimensional Quality Audit in §10.1.1 redefines UI/UX as content/copy quality while §10.1 already scores build-quality UI/UX; no conflict-resolution rule is stated for when the same finding appears under both, and the folding formula in §7.6 simply unions them without deduplication.

allObjections.title: purpose_record schema truncated
allObjections.detail: §7.5 adds purpose_record as the 7th block with a JSON schema that ends mid-array at fulfillment_signals; no validation, required-field, or atomic-write rule is provided, unlike the explicit atomicity guarantee for delta_log in the same section.

allObjections.title: §27 gate depends on parked CAs
allObjections.detail: CA-15-D makes the end-stage SSOT-conformance test a hard gate, yet the proposal repeatedly cross-references parked CA-13 and CA-14 entries that are explicitly NOT in §18.4; no fallback or version-pin is defined if those amendments remain unratified.

adversarial.worse_than_status_quo: The 7-axis quality audit with equal weighting in §7.6 means a product with perfect functionality but minor grammar issues could score lower than a broken product with perfect grammar, incentivizing surface polish over core functionality.
adversarial.precedent: Google's Panda algorithm update (2011) initially over-weighted content quality signals like grammar and readability, causing high-quality technical documentation sites to rank below content farms with better prose, until they rebalanced the signals.

perReviewer.rejection_steelman: This proposal should be deferred until CA-13 and CA-14 are resolved, as it builds scoring mechanisms on top of an unstable foundation. The 75-vs-95 threshold debate in CA-13 directly impacts how these quality axes are weighted, and CA-14's Phase A/B distinction affects when quality audits run. Building a 7-axis rubric before establishing the basic scoring threshold and phase gates risks significant rework and creates more parked amendments.

CA-15-A-Q1.pick_text: REJECT — none of the listed options is acceptable as specified
CA-15-A-Q1.rationale: The proposed 7 axes have unclear boundaries (UX vs Accessibility overlap) and the 'Observability' axis is undefined in the proposal, making conformance testing impossible.

CA-15-A-Q2.pick_text: Subordinate to Five-Layer — Multi-Dim rubric becomes telemetry feeding §7.6 score, not equal footing.
CA-15-A-Q2.rationale: Equal footing creates the double-counting problem identified in objection 1; subordination allows the rubric to inform without distorting the score.

CA-15-A-Q3.pick_text: Knob exists but admin-role only (operator cannot disable axes).
CA-15-A-Q3.rationale: Allowing operators to disable quality axes defeats the purpose of standardized quality assessment; admin-only preserves override capability for exceptional cases.

CA-15-B-Q1.pick_text: Ratify but optional — `purpose_record` exists but is not required.
CA-15-B-Q1.rationale: Making purpose_record required creates the race condition identified in objection 2; optional allows gradual adoption without blocking core functionality.

CA-15-B-Q2.pick_text: Ratify 2 — drop reverse-engineered (risk of poisoning SSOT with wrong inferred intent).
CA-15-B-Q2.rationale: Reverse-engineering purpose from crawled content is unreliable and risks encoding incorrect assumptions into the canonical record.

CA-15-B-Q3.pick_text: Reject regex — placeholder detection belongs in linter, not canonical.
CA-15-B-Q3.rationale: Hard-coding specific placeholder patterns in the canonical spec creates maintenance burden; this validation belongs in tooling layer.

CA-15-C-Q1.pick_text: Floor only — keep numeric threshold, drop purpose-fulfillment exit.
CA-15-C-Q1.rationale: Purpose-fulfillment scoring is too subjective and untestable compared to numeric thresholds; mixing subjective and objective gates weakens the entire system.

CA-15-C-Q2.pick_text: REJECT — none of the listed options is acceptable as specified
CA-15-C-Q2.rationale: The proposal never defines how purpose_fulfillment_score is calculated, making any threshold meaningless.

CA-15-C-Q3.pick_text: Block instead — PURPOSE_DRIFT halts the run, requires operator re-capture.
CA-15-C-Q3.rationale: Silently continuing with drifted purpose risks optimizing toward outdated goals; explicit operator intervention ensures alignment.

CA-15-D-Q1.pick_text: Downgrade §27 to advisory — surfaces conformance issues but does not block.
CA-15-D-Q1.rationale: Hard-gating on SSOT conformance when the SSOT itself is rapidly evolving (10+ CAs pending) creates deadlock; advisory mode provides value without blocking progress.

CA-15-D-Q2.pick_text: Partial — CEO sign-off invalidates only on CA promotions affecting §27.
CA-15-D-Q2.rationale: Blanket invalidation on every CA creates the operational burden identified in objection 3; scoped invalidation balances compliance with practicality.

perReviewer.overallNotes: The proposal attempts to address real gaps but introduces more complexity than it resolves, particularly around overlapping quality dimensions and undefined scoring mechanisms.

objections.title: Overly complex quality audit
objections.detail: The 7-axis Multi-Dimensional Quality Audit in CA-15-A seems overly complex and potentially subjective. The conformance test acceptance criteria for each axis rely on precision/recall thresholds against labeled corpora, which may be difficult to create and maintain, especially for axes like 'UI/UX' and 'Other'.

objections.title: Purpose capture ambiguity
objections.detail: The purpose capture modes in CA-15-B, particularly 'inferred' and 'synthesized', rely heavily on LLM inference, which can be unreliable and lead to inaccurate or biased purpose statements. The lack of clear guidelines for LLM synthesis could result in inconsistent and unpredictable purpose capture.

objections.title: SSOT-conformance gate risk
objections.detail: The SSOT-conformance gate in CA-15-D, while intended to ensure adherence to the SSOT, could become a bottleneck in the development process. The requirement for CEO re-sign-off on every CA promotion could create delays and hinder agility, especially if the CEO is unavailable or has limited bandwidth.

objections.title: Extensibility axis 'Other' vague
objections.detail: The 'Other' axis in the Multi-Dimensional Quality Audit (CA-15-A) is a catch-all that lacks clear definition. While intended for extensibility, it could become a dumping ground for subjective or irrelevant findings, undermining the overall rigor of the audit.

objections.title: Purpose drift handling unclear
objections.detail: The handling of `PURPOSE_DRIFT` in CA-15-C is unclear. Exiting with `NO_IMPROVEMENT` and an annotation seems insufficient. A significant drift in purpose should trigger a more proactive response, such as requiring operator intervention or automatically re-running the purpose capture process.

adversarial.worse_than_status_quo: The SSOT-conformance gate (CA-15-D) with mandatory CEO re-sign-off on every CA promotion could create a significant bottleneck, slowing down development and deployment cycles. This could lead to frustration among developers and operators, and ultimately reduce the overall efficiency of the FlowAI system.

perReviewer.rejection_steelman: This proposal introduces significant complexity with the multi-dimensional quality audit and purpose capture mechanisms. The reliance on LLMs for purpose inference and the potential for bottlenecks with the SSOT-conformance gate raise concerns about the practicality and maintainability of the proposed changes. Deferring this proposal would allow for further refinement and validation of these concepts before implementation.

CA-15-A-Q1.pick_text: Adopt different axis set entirely (specify in rationale).
CA-15-A-Q1.rationale: A more focused set of axes, such as UX, API, Data, Auth, Perf, Accessibility, and Observability, would provide a more actionable and measurable assessment of quality. This aligns better with the existing 5-dimension scoring engine and avoids the subjectivity of axes like 'Grammar' and 'Syntax'.

CA-15-A-Q2.pick_text: Subordinate to Five-Layer — Multi-Dim rubric becomes telemetry feeding §7.6 score, not equal footing.
CA-15-A-Q2.rationale: The Multi-Dim rubric should inform the §7.6 score but not be on equal footing. The Five-Layer framework represents core system qualities, while the Multi-Dim rubric captures more subjective content-related aspects. Treating them as separate inputs allows for a more nuanced understanding of overall quality.

CA-15-A-Q3.pick_text: Knob exists but admin-role only (operator cannot disable axes).
CA-15-A-Q3.rationale: Per-axis enable/disable knobs should be restricted to admin roles to maintain consistency and prevent operators from inadvertently disabling critical quality checks. This ensures that all products undergo a baseline level of quality assessment.

CA-15-B-Q1.pick_text: Ratify but optional — `purpose_record` exists but is not required.
CA-15-B-Q1.rationale: While capturing the purpose of a product is valuable, making the `purpose_record` mandatory for every product may be too restrictive. Allowing it to be optional provides flexibility for cases where the purpose is self-evident or not easily captured.

CA-15-B-Q2.pick_text: Ratify 2 — drop reverse-engineered (risk of poisoning SSOT with wrong inferred intent).
CA-15-B-Q2.rationale: The 'reverse-engineered' purpose capture mode carries a significant risk of poisoning the SSOT with inaccurate or biased intent. Dropping this mode reduces the potential for misrepresenting the true purpose of a product.

CA-15-B-Q3.pick_text: Reject regex — placeholder detection belongs in linter, not canonical.
CA-15-B-Q3.rationale: Placeholder detection is better suited for a linter or code quality tool, rather than being enforced as part of the canonical SSOT schema. This keeps the SSOT focused on core purpose capture and avoids adding unnecessary complexity.

CA-15-C-Q1.rationale: The two-step exit, combining a numeric floor with purpose-fulfillment as the north-star, provides a balanced approach to optimization. It ensures a minimum level of quality while also aligning the product with its intended purpose.

CA-15-C-Q2.rationale: A default threshold of 0.7 for the `purpose_fulfillment_score` strikes a reasonable balance between rigor and flexibility. It provides a starting point for evaluating purpose fulfillment without being overly restrictive.

CA-15-C-Q3.pick_text: Block instead — PURPOSE_DRIFT halts the run, requires operator re-capture.
CA-15-C-Q3.rationale: A significant drift in purpose should halt the run and require operator intervention to re-capture the purpose. This ensures that the optimization process is aligned with the current intent of the product.

CA-15-D-Q1.pick_text: Downgrade §27 to advisory — surfaces conformance issues but does not block.
CA-15-D-Q1.rationale: The SSOT-conformance gate should be downgraded to advisory to avoid creating a bottleneck in the development process. Surfacing conformance issues without blocking allows for continuous improvement without hindering agility.

CA-15-D-Q2.pick_text: Reject — CEO sign-off is per-product, not per-CA-promotion.
CA-15-D-Q2.rationale: CEO sign-off should be per-product, not per-CA-promotion, to avoid unnecessary delays and administrative overhead. Requiring CEO re-sign-off on every CA promotion is overly burdensome and does not provide significant additional value.

perReviewer.overallNotes: This proposal introduces several complex mechanisms that require careful consideration. While the goals of improving quality and aligning with purpose are commendable, the potential for bottlenecks and the reliance on subjective assessments raise concerns about the practicality and maintainability of the proposed changes.

objections.title: Axis set mismatches question
objections.detail: CA-15-A-Q1 asks to ratify a 7-axis rubric with UX, API, Data, Auth, Perf, Accessibility, Observability, but the proposal text defines axes as redundancy, grammar, syntax, UI/UX-content, legal, privacy, and other. That mismatch makes the amendment internally inconsistent with its own acceptance criterion and untestable as written.

objections.title: Duplicate scoring semantics
objections.detail: CA-15-A folds the new audit into §7.6 with the same score formula and equal footing with existing detectors, but it also says the axes are content-quality and separately says they are advisory in the legal axis. The proposal does not define how conflicts are resolved when content-quality findings, Phase A findings, and Phase B findings all overlap, so the same defect can be double-counted or suppressed depending on implementation choice.

objections.title: Purpose capture risks false intent
objections.detail: CA-15-B lets the system infer or synthesize a product's purpose from crawls or multiple sources and then stores that as canonical ProductSSOT state. That creates a high risk of ossifying a model hallucination or a marketing page's incidental text as the product's real objective, especially when the operator never supplied a precise purpose statement.

objections.title: Drift gate can deadlock runs
objections.detail: CA-15-C's PURPOSE_DRIFT semantics can exit NO_IMPROVEMENT with explicit drift annotation when the purpose changes, but it does not require a fresh operator approval path or a bounded fallback. A product whose legitimate scope changes during renewal could repeatedly fail the exit gate even after successful technical remediation, turning an optimization loop into a deadlock.

objections.title: CEO re-sign every CA is brittle
objections.detail: CA-15-D-Q2 makes CEO sign-off invalid on every CA promotion, even promotions that do not affect the specific conformance gate. This couples ordinary governance churn to a single human approver and can stall the entire pipeline over unrelated amendments, creating an availability bottleneck rather than a control mechanism.

adversarial.worse_than_status_quo: If purpose is auto-inferred from a clone's landing page and then used to judge future renewals, the system can lock onto the wrong intent and repeatedly 'optimize' toward the wrong outcome. Compared with the status quo of operator-stated or minimally modeled intent, this can make good products look noncompliant and block beneficial changes.
adversarial.precedent: OpenAI Structured Outputs and many JSON-schema tool-calling systems have shown that forcing structure does not prevent semantic errors; malformed or mis-modeled intent still gets serialized cleanly. More directly, the long-running problem of 'garbage in, garbage out' in intake forms and knowledge bases applies here: canonical storage of inferred intent often hardens mistakes instead of correcting them.

perReviewer.rejection_steelman: The strongest case for rejecting or deferring CA-15 is that it expands the canonical SSOT surface before the existing governance model has a stable, unambiguous way to validate it. The amendment introduces new canonical data, new scoring dimensions, and new blocking gates simultaneously, but does not fully specify precedence, conflict resolution, or rollback when the new signals disagree. Deferring until the axis list, purpose-capture authority, and drift-handling semantics are reconciled would reduce the risk of locking the pipeline into a brittle or self-contradictory standard.

CA-15-A-Q1.pick_text: REJECT — none of the listed options is acceptable as specified
CA-15-A-Q1.rationale: The listed options are for a different axis set than the amendment text: the question names UX, API, Data, Auth, Perf, Accessibility, Observability, while the draft defines redundancy, grammar, syntax, UI/UX-content, legal, privacy, and other. Because the option set does not match the proposal, none can be accepted as specified.

CA-15-A-Q2.pick_text: Subordinate to Five-Layer — Multi-Dim rubric becomes telemetry feeding §7.6 score, not equal footing.
CA-15-A-Q2.rationale: Equal-footing folding invites double-counting and makes the score harder to interpret when §10, §6, and Phase B all report overlapping defects. Subordination preserves the rubric as useful telemetry without letting it become a second, partially redundant gate.

CA-15-A-Q3.pick_text: Knob exists but admin-role only (operator cannot disable axes).
CA-15-A-Q3.rationale: Per-axis disabling by operators would let submitters selectively suppress hard-to-satisfy findings and game the score. Restricting the control to admin roles keeps auditability while preventing score manipulation.

CA-15-B-Q1.pick_text: Reject — purpose lives in operator-stated spec, not in ProductSSOT canonical schema.
CA-15-B-Q1.rationale: Purpose is a human intent statement and should remain the operator's responsibility rather than being frozen as canonical system state. Storing it canonically as a required block risks treating inferred or stale intent as authoritative.

CA-15-B-Q2.rationale: Different entry paths do need different capture modes, and the triad matches the proposal's onboarding paths. The risk is not the existence of modes but the need for stronger provenance and review around inferred or synthesized purposes.

CA-15-B-Q3.pick_text: Expand regex — add more placeholder patterns (e.g. "PLACEHOLDER", "XXX", "TBD").
CA-15-B-Q3.rationale: Placeholder rejection should cover the obvious variants if it is meant to protect canonical purpose text from empty defaults. The current regex is too narrow to catch common placeholder leakage.

CA-15-C-Q1.rationale: A pure north-star or pure floor is too rigid; the run should require purpose progress but also preserve a measurable minimum quality floor. The draft needs a clearer fallback when purpose shifts legitimately during the run.

CA-15-C-Q2.rationale: A universal threshold is too blunt because purpose clarity varies by product maturity and input type. Defaulting to 0.7 is acceptable only if admins can tune it per product or pipeline class.

CA-15-C-Q3.rationale: Pure NO_IMPROVEMENT exit on drift is too passive because it may hide a real scope change, while hard-blocking every drift can deadlock legitimate updates. The semantics should distinguish minor drift, intentional re-scope, and accidental mismatch.

CA-15-D-Q1.pick_text: Ratify §27 as drafted — end-stage SSOT-conformance test is a hard gate.
CA-15-D-Q1.rationale: An end-stage hard gate is a reasonable control point if the SSOT is truly the acceptance spec. Making it advisory would weaken the whole purpose of conformance checking.

CA-15-D-Q2.rationale: Re-signing should be required only when the relevant acceptance or governance surface changes, not for every CA promotion. Narrowing invalidation avoids unnecessary human bottlenecks while preserving sign-off on materially affected controls.

perReviewer.overallNotes: I am voting with several deferrals/partial modifications because the draft mixes governance, scoring, and provenance changes without fully specifying precedence and provenance rules. The biggest issue is that the question set and the amendment text are not consistently aligned, which makes several items impossible to ratify as written.

objections.title: Overly Complex Quality Audit
objections.detail: The 7-axis Multi-Dimensional Quality Audit (§10.1.1) introduces multiple new dimensions that may be redundant or difficult to calibrate. For example, 'UI/UX' and 'Legal' may overlap in certain cases, and the 'Other' axis is too vague.

objections.title: Purpose Capture Ambiguity
objections.detail: The three canonical purpose-capture modes (§7.5 `purpose_record`) may lead to inconsistent purpose statements. The 'inferred' mode relies on LLM inference, which may not always accurately capture the operator's intent.

objections.title: SSOT-Conformance Gate Timing
objections.detail: The §27 SSOT-Conformance Gate is placed at the end-stage, which may allow non-conformant changes to propagate through the pipeline. It should be considered to run this gate at every §11 step.

adversarial.worse_than_status_quo: If the Multi-Dimensional Quality Audit flags too many false positives, it could lead to an excessive number of findings, making it difficult for operators to address them, and potentially causing a decrease in overall product quality due to alert fatigue.
adversarial.precedent: The introduction of multiple audit dimensions has caused issues in other AI systems, such as the Google AI Overviews, where the complexity of the audit criteria led to unintended consequences and required significant recalibration.

perReviewer.rejection_steelman: The proposal introduces significant changes to the existing pipeline, including a complex new quality audit mechanism and a new purpose capture system. These changes may interact with existing components in unforeseen ways, potentially destabilizing the system. It would be prudent to defer this proposal until more thorough testing and simulation can be conducted to mitigate these risks.

perReviewer.overallNotes: The proposal is comprehensive but introduces significant complexity; careful monitoring and potential adjustments will be necessary.

objections.title: §10.1.1 rubric overlaps §10.1
objections.detail: The 7-axis Multi-Dimensional Quality Audit in §10.1.1 redefines UI/UX as content/copy quality while §10.1 already scores build-quality UI/UX; no conflict-resolution rule is stated for when the same finding appears under both, and the folding formula in §7.6 simply unions them without deduplication.

objections.title: purpose_record schema truncated
objections.detail: §7.5 adds purpose_record as the 7th block with a JSON schema that ends mid-array at fulfillment_signals; no validation, required-field, or atomic-write rule is provided, unlike the explicit atomicity guarantee for delta_log in the same section.

objections.title: §27 gate depends on parked CAs
objections.detail: CA-15-D makes the end-stage SSOT-conformance test a hard gate, yet the proposal repeatedly cross-references parked CA-13 and CA-14 entries that are explicitly NOT in §18.4; no fallback or version-pin is defined if those amendments remain unratified.

adversarial.worse_than_status_quo: Adding per-axis disable knobs and purpose-driven exits without a mandatory human review step for disabled axes or PURPOSE_DRIFT could silently suppress critical legal/privacy findings or allow runs to exit on stale purpose text, producing lower-quality outputs than the current §7.6 surface-only scoring that at least forces every issue to a terminal decision.

perReviewer.rejection_steelman: The proposal bundles four new mechanisms (7-axis rubric, purpose_record block, purpose north-star exit, and §27 gate) on top of an already complex Self-Governance Layer while several prerequisite amendments remain parked below quorum; ratifying it now risks creating an inconsistent canonical reference that later requires costly rollback or re-numbering of entries.
